title: Interleaved prefill-decode pipeline and kernel coalescing to reduce tail latency
author: Leah Kim
release_notes: Introduce interleaved prefill-decode scheduling and kernel coalescing to improve tail latency and throughput for mixed short/long workloads. Opt-in via feature flag; no API change.
description: Motivation: In high-concurrency mixed workloads we observed recurring tail latency spikes when prefill chunk boundaries synchronized poorly with decode work and kernel launches were fragmented across tiny micro-batches. This PR introduces an interleaving scheduler and a kernel coalescing layer that let decode start earlier and group adjacent kernel invocations to amortize launch overhead. Goals: reduce p99/p999 latency, improve throughput for short and medium sequence workloads, and avoid regressions on long-form generation. Summary of changes: 1) stage-interleaver scheduler: schedules prefill and decode tasks on the same GPU worker in a fine-grained round-robin when prefill progress crosses a configurable watermark (prefill_watermark_ms). This allows decode to begin as soon as the first chunk arrives rather than waiting for full prefill completion. 2) kernel coalescer: runtime/kernel_coalescer.cpp groups compatible kernel calls (same op, compatible dtypes and seq lengths) originating from different pipeline stages within the same dispatch tick; coalescing is conservative and respects memory headroom heuristics. 3) prefill chunk metadata: prefill chunks now carry a compact token-range watermark and KV signatures so the decode stage can perform safe speculative KV reads and early KV cache lookups. 4) KV shard-awareness: KV cache eviction and soft-evict heuristics were updated to avoid evicting shards currently used by in-flight interleaved decodes. 5) Batching policy updates: continuous batching now maintains micro-batch windows per stage to allow bounded cross-stage coalescing without increasing tail latency. 6) Observability: new metrics (runtime.prefill_watermark_latency, runtime.kernel_coalesce_count, runtime.interleave_slices) and a small dashboard patch. Tests & bench: unit tests for the coalescer, scheduler integration tests in tests/runtime_interleave_test.py, and microbench harness updates in tools/benchmarks/prefill_decode. Benchmarks (internal mixed-short workload): median token latency -6.1%, p95 -9.8%, p99 -12.3%, throughput +29% when kernel coalescing enabled; worst-case memory overhead <3% for our test matrix. Rollout: feature flag runtime.enable_interleaved_prefill (default off). Canary rollout to dedicated pool followed by gradual percentage ramp. Backwards compatibility: no API changes, KV cache format unchanged; flag-controlled. Checklist: - [x] scheduler + coalescer design doc linked in Linear - [x] unit/integration tests - [x] benchmark harness updates - [x] feature flag + fallback path - [x] observability & dashboards - [x] small canary and SLA watchlist Commits summary: see commits list below. Changed files (high level): runtime/scheduler/stage_interleaver.cpp, runtime/kernel/kernel_coalescer.cpp, runtime/kv/kv_shard_manager.cpp, runtime/kv/prefill_metadata.h, tools/benchmarks/prefill_decode_bench.py, tests/runtime_interleave_test.py, docs/perf/prefill_decode_interleave.md, scripts/canary_rollout.sh, build/meson.build (runtime entries), ci/runtime_integration.yml. Review notes: initial CI run flagged a flaky integration test (interleave timing); fixed by adding deterministic tick injection in test harness. Memory safety and race conditions were carefully audited; sanitizer runs were clean on our CI hardware. Merge: squash and merge after approvers signed off.

discussion: Marcus Reed: Overall this is promising; main concern is memory pressure when coalescing in worst-case burst traffic. Can we bound coalescing by a soft memory budget?

Leah Kim: We implemented a soft headroom budget that refuses coalescing beyond a percentage of free GPU memory; fallback is immediate dispatch. See kernel_coalescer.cpp heuristics and the new metric runtime.kernel_coalesce_skipped_by_mem.
Priya Nair: How does this interact with KV cache eviction? I worry about thrashing on small KV shards.

Leah Kim: Added shard-awareness to soft-evict and a short lock window to prevent eviction of shards referenced by in-flight interleaved decodes. See kv_shard_manager.cpp changes and tests in runtime_interleave_test.py.
